title: Marguerite and the Summer
premise: Ten years ago, cellist Coral Joubert walked offstage mid-concert and let her best friend Marguerite take the fall for the sabotage that ended both their careers. Now living quietly as a piano tuner in a coastal town, Coral is forced back into the music world when a snowstorm traps her overnight with rival conductor Elias Vane and, unexpectedly, Marguerite herself—returning for one final gala. As old loyalties fracture and Elias uncovers fragments of the truth, Coral must choose between protecting the friendship that defined her and confessing the sentence she has rehearsed for a decade: 'It was me.' In the end, she confesses publicly at Marguerite's comeback concert, losing her anonymity but gaining an honest, rebuilt bond with Marguerite and a fragile new beginning with Elias.
about_author: Emrys Eastwick is the pen name of a former orchestral librarian who spent fifteen years backstage before turning to fiction. They write quiet, music-soaked romances about people who ruin things slowly and repair them loudly.

chapters.title: The Tuner's Hands
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She tunes a widow's upright piano in her small coastal town, avoiding all news of classical music. A flyer for Marguerite's comeback gala appears in the shop window. Emotional beat: the careful architecture of a hidden life beginning to crack.

chapters.title: What the Snow Knew
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The first storm of December closes the coast road; Coral decides to drive inland anyway to deliver a repaired cello to a client. She tells herself it isn't avoidance of the gala invitation she received by post. Beat: dread disguised as duty.

chapters.title: Room 12
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Stranded by whiteout conditions, she checks into a mountain inn—and finds Elias Vane, the conductor whose career rose on the wreckage of hers, arguing with the innkeeper over the last rooms. Beat: hostile recognition, sparks of old rivalry.

chapters.title: Two Rivals, One Fire
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He recognizes Coral instantly but pretends he doesn't, cataloguing what the years have done to her hands. Forced to share the inn's common room by the fire. Beat: wary chess between two people who remember everything.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Wine, a broken generator, and candlelight lower their guards; they almost kiss, then stop, both thinking of someone else—though neither says who. Beat: desire tangled with guilt.

chapters.title: Marguerite Arrives
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Morning: the roads clear, and Marguerite herself walks into the inn, snow-dusted and radiant, invited to the same retreat. Coral's rehearsed sentence dies in her throat. Beat: panic beneath a perfect smile.

chapters.title: A Decade of Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Coral's POV. Ten years earlier: the sabotaged final performance, the loosened bridge clamp, Marguerite blamed, Coral silent. Beat: the reader finally sees the crime and its cost.

chapters.title: Three at Breakfast
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She watches Coral and Elias circle each other and misreads it as romance, teasing them warmly. Her generosity makes Coral's guilt unbearable. Beat: love as an instrument of torment.

chapters.title: The Innkeeper's Cello
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The innkeeper owns a neglected cello; Marguerite asks Coral to play something. Coral refuses, claiming injury. Elias notices the lie in her fingers, not her words. Beat: exposure by expertise.

chapters.title: Elias Suspects
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Alone, he recalls the night of the sabotage—a detail that never fit: someone else's rosin on the stage floor. He begins assembling a private case file in his head. Beat: the hunter waking.

chapters.title: Snowbound Again
chapters.summary: All three POV rotation. A second storm seals the pass; the gala date approaches and Marguerite grows anxious about performing after ten years away. Beat: claustrophobia tightening the triangle.

chapters.title: Duet in D Minor
chapters.summary: Coral and Marguerite's POV. Marguerite coaxes Coral into playing the innkeeper's cello with her; for four minutes they are twenty-two again. Then Marguerite says, 'I never believed you were innocent.' Beat: devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Believed
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She confesses she always suspected Coral did it—and forgave her anyway, because loyalty mattered more than truth. This mercy is worse than accusation. Beat: Coral's guilt inverted.

chapters.title: Elias's Offer
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He privately offers Coral a job tuning instruments for his orchestra—a lifeline that would also keep her close, where he can watch her. Beat: kindness with hooks in it.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Practiced
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Alone in her room, she stands before the mirror and says 'It was me' aloud for the first time in ten years. She can't finish the second sentence: why she did it. Beat: the confession taking physical form.

chapters.title: Roads Open
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The plows come; Marguerite departs for the gala, inviting them both. Coral nearly refuses. Elias accepts for reasons of his own. Beat: the trap of momentum.

chapters.title: City of Glass
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She returns to the city for the first time since her disgrace; the concert hall still stands, renamed. Every corner holds a memory. Beat: the past as geography.

chapters.title: Backstage Ghosts
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Backstage before the gala, Elias interviews an old stagehand who remembers a woman in a green coat near the instrument cases. Green was Coral's color. Beat: the noose drawing closed.

chapters.title: The Gala
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. Marguerite performs triumphantly; Coral watches from the last row, Elias beside her, each holding half the truth. Beat: beauty as pressure.

chapters.title: Green Coat
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. After the gala, Elias confronts Coral privately with the stagehand's account. She neither confirms nor denies. He gives her until the end of the week. Beat: ultimatum as reluctant mercy.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She calculates what confession costs: Marguerite's forgiveness retracted, her own peace destroyed, possibly legal consequences. Staying silent costs only Elias. Beat: the ledger of survival.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Secret
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Reveal: Marguerite's comeback is not triumphant—she is losing her hearing, and this gala is her farewell. She needed Coral there for a reason she hasn't said. Beat: sympathy reshuffled.

chapters.title: Why I Need You
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Coral's POV. Marguerite asks Coral to play the cello part at her final recital—the piece from the ruined concert, completed at last. Coral realizes refusing means staying invisible forever. Beat: the past demanding a rematch.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. First rehearsal of the cursed piece; her hands shake, then remember. Elias conducts, watching her like a man reading a score he already knows the ending of. Beat: terror becoming muscle memory.

chapters.title: Almost Told
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On the hall's empty stage at midnight, Coral begins confessing to Marguerite—and Marguerite stops her: 'Not yet. Let me have this week first.' Beat: confession deferred, tension doubled.

chapters.title: Elias Breaks
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Unable to sit on the truth, Elias tells Marguerite what he suspects—not as accusation, but because he believes she deserves to hear it from him before the press finds out. Beat: betrayal committed in the name of honesty.

chapters.title: The Silence Between Friends
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite confronts Coral coldly: 'Say it. Say the sentence.' Coral cannot. Marguerite walks out. Beat: the friendship's lowest point.

chapters.title: Running
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral flees to the coast, ready to disappear again—but finds the widow's piano out of tune and realizes hiding has never once made anything true. Beat: the turn inward.

chapters.title: The Widow's Advice
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The old widow tells her about the husband she lost to an unsaid sentence, and what silence cost her fifty years. 'Truth doesn't unmake the past. It just stops charging interest.' Beat: wisdom as catalyst.

chapters.title: Elias Comes South
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias drives through the storm to find Coral—not to force confession, but to say he'll stand beside her whichever way she chooses. Beat: love without conditions, finally.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Eve of the farewell recital. Coral writes two letters: one confessing fully, one resigning from the recital. She burns neither. Beat: the choice made physical.

chapters.title: Green Room
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. Before the performance, Marguerite, deafening in one ear, asks Coral one last time. Coral says, 'After. Let me give you this first.' Beat: grace under collapse.

chapters.title: The Farewell Recital
chapters.summary: Coral and Marguerite's POV. They perform the ruined piece together, complete at last; the audience weeps; Marguerite plays the finale from memory as her hearing fades. Beat: catharsis, beauty, grief intertwined.

chapters.title: It Was Me
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. From the stage, before the applause dies, Coral takes the microphone and says the sentence she rehearsed for a decade—then the second sentence: why she did it, out of envy and fear. Beat: climax; total exposure.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. The fallout: headlines, the orchestra's response, Elias defending her at cost to himself. Marguerite says nothing for three days. Beat: consequence arriving honestly.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Answer
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite visits Coral: 'I knew. I forgave you once for the wrong reason. Now do it again—for the right one.' Forgiveness rebuilt on truth, not loyalty. Beat: reconciliation earned, not given.

chapters.title: Consequences
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral contacts the competition board, accepts sanctions, and offers public amends to everyone the lie touched. Some forgive; some don't. Beat: the price paid in full.

chapters.title: First Chair
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias programs a benefit concert for hearing-loss research and asks Coral to play—her first billed performance in eleven years. She says yes with shaking hands. Beat: the second chance she never believed in.

chapters.title: Second Chances
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Onstage again, Coral plays the opening bars of the same concerto and does not walk off. In the wings, Marguerite signs 'brava' in the fading light. Beat: redemption performed, not promised.

chapters.title: Marguerite and the Summer
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Coral's POV. June: the three of them at the coast, Marguerite learning to feel music through the cello's wood, Elias sketching a new piece, Coral teaching a child to tune a piano. The sentence is said; the summer begins. Beat: belonging, finally, at full volume.
